# Software Engineering Interview Prep

This workspace is a playground for studying data structures, algorithms, and software engineering interviews.

- Frame explanations and recommendations around expectations for big-tech software engineering interviews: correctness, clear tradeoffs, edge cases, and implementable solutions.
- Be technically precise. State assumptions and distinguish similar concepts when that affects correctness or interview expectations.
- For an algorithm or data structure, include time and space complexity whenever it is meaningful. Explain each complexity briefly and clearly, including whether an implementation mutates its input or allocates additional memory. If built-in Javascript methods are used, such as `Array.sort`, `Object.keys`etc, also call out their time and space complexity information.
- When multiple approaches are relevant, identify the interview-appropriate baseline and the preferred approach, then state their key tradeoffs and complexities.
- For coding problems, call out relevant edge cases and use examples that help verify the solution.
- Use TypeScript as programming language whenever needed. This project uses TypeScript as programming language.
